title: SlideCast Studio v4.2 “TATE”
subtitle: Update — vertical subtitles, vertical speech bubbles and editable acting assets
description: SlideCast Studio v4.2 TATE adds a text direction setting for vertical subtitles and speech bubbles, vertical band placement and Latin character orientation, vertical badges and text stickers with inner padding, three new expressions, and editing of acting assets after import.
author: aokuma
hero_alt: SlideCast Studio v4.2 TATE — Subtitles and bubbles, set vertically.
source_note: See the note article for later additions and comments.

blocks.title: 🌐 About the screenshots
blocks.text: The interface screenshots on this page use the Japanese edition. The English captions explain the relevant controls and behaviour. “TATE” (縦) means vertical writing, the traditional Japanese layout that reads from top to bottom and right to left.

blocks.html:
SlideCast Studio has been updated to v4.2 “TATE”.

The previous release, v4.1 “FRAME”, let you refine the image, character and subtitle layout on each slide. This release focuses on making videos that present their text vertically.

Vertical writing suits literary and traditional Japanese material: narrated novels and essays, haiku and tanka, product introductions in a Japanese style, language teaching material, and manga-style dialogue. You can switch to it without redoing your horizontal settings.

sections.title: Set subtitles and speech bubbles vertically
sections.intro: The Subtitle tab of the settings dialog now has a text direction setting.

blocks.html: Choose between horizontal (as before) and vertical. The switch applies to both the subtitle band and the speech bubbles of your characters. Font, text size, colour, outline and shadow settings carry over unchanged.

blocks.alt: The text direction control in the Subtitle tab set to vertical, with the preview beside it
blocks.caption: Selecting the vertical option (文字の方向 → 縦書き) turns the subtitle in the preview vertical straight away

blocks.title: 🔒 Horizontal remains the default
blocks.text: Existing projects open exactly as before. Switch only the projects you want to present vertically.

blocks.html: Simple mode shows a note on screen when a project is set to vertical. Change the direction and placement from the Subtitle tab in the detailed settings.

sections.title: Place the vertical band on the left, centre or right
sections.intro: In vertical mode the position controls change to their vertical equivalents.

blocks.html: The vertical band position can be set to left, centre or right; right is the default. Japanese vertical text reads from right to left, so the default already reads naturally. Centre suits a single short line placed in the middle of the frame. For the left and right positions, the side margin (0–500px) sets the distance from the edge of the frame.

blocks.alt: Vertical position settings: band position, bubble vertical alignment, vertical padding and band width
blocks.caption: Vertical mode offers band position (左・中央・右 = left, centre, right), band width and vertical padding

blocks.text: A left/right split layout is supported too

blocks.html: With the separated layout, vertical mode presents it as a left/right split: the subtitle takes one side of the frame and the visuals fill the rest. It keeps subtitles off your documents and photos while staying vertical.

blocks.title: ⚠️ When the text does not fit the band
blocks.text: The settings screen shows a warning asking you to split the script or adjust the text size. Split the script, or revisit the text size and band width.

sections.title: Choose how numbers and Latin letters appear
sections.intro: A new setting offers three ways to present Latin characters inside vertical text.

items.title: Automatic
items.text: One digit upright, two digits combined into the line; other Latin runs rotated (default)

items.title: Upright, one by one
items.text: Every character stands upright, stacked down the line

items.title: Rotated as a run
items.text: Words and URLs stay together and turn on their side

blocks.alt: The same sentence rendered with each of the three Latin character options
blocks.caption: The same sentence, with numbers and Latin words presented differently by each option

blocks.html:
The default is Automatic, which keeps dates and quantities such as “2026年” and “10月” easy to read. Choose the rotated option when a product name or URL should stay legible as a word, and the upright option when numbers or symbols should line up one per row.

Punctuation, small kana, brackets and the long vowel mark are drawn in their vertical positions and orientations as well.

sections.title: Badges and text stickers can be vertical as well
sections.intro: The text direction setting is also available for badges and text stickers.

blocks.html: As with subtitles, you set the direction and the Latin character treatment individually. Place a vertical title in a corner of the frame, or add a vertical label beside a document. You can also keep subtitles horizontal and make only the stickers vertical.

blocks.alt: A frame with a vertical badge and a vertical text sticker
blocks.caption: A vertical title badge and a vertical sticker label combined with a vertical subtitle

blocks.html:
Badges and text stickers gained horizontal padding and vertical padding settings. Both accept 60%–160% in 5% steps and default to 100%, so text can sit tightly inside its background or breathe more.

When you resize a text sticker by dragging its edge, the padding is preserved as the text rewraps and scales.

blocks.title: 🔒 Existing data is unchanged
blocks.text: Items saved before this release keep their previous appearance.

sections.title: Surprised, troubled and thinking join the expressions
sections.intro: With happy, sad and angry, six expressions are now available.

blocks.html: Characters gained the surprised, troubled and thinking expressions. Automatic acting can pick them up from the wording of a line.

blocks.title: 🔒 Existing characters look the same
blocks.text: Only the happy expression is enabled automatically, as before, and an expression without artwork is never used.
Replace acting assets one frame at a time

blocks.html: Character settings gained an acting assets panel for expressions and gestures, so material imported from a MouthLoop character pack can be edited later.

items: Replace a single expression frame
Add an expression from six images of your own, or from a ZIP
Add a gesture (2–60 frames, up to three gestures)
Change a gesture’s display name and frame duration
Delete material you no longer need

blocks.alt: The acting assets panel in character settings, listing expressions with buttons to add expressions and gestures
blocks.caption: Register expressions in the same order as the six base frames (eyes open, mouth closed → eyes closed, mouth open). A ZIP can be selected directly

blocks.html: You can add a missing expression without rebuilding the whole pack, and the same panel is available from character settings in Simple mode. MouthLoop’s expression set only covers smiling, sad and angry, so for surprised, troubled and thinking, build the face in MouthLoop by setting the master image’s expression to free text, then add that material here. Any acting that referenced deleted material falls back to the standard presentation.

sections.title: Speech bubble and subtitle fixes
sections.intro: Vertical support came with a review of how speech bubbles are drawn.

items: Fixed an unnatural tail growing from the top edge of a wide bubble towards a character in the upper left
Limited the tail length to 45% of the shorter side and joined its base with a curve
Fixed an abrupt length change when the tail adjustment was set to zero
Fixed vertical bubbles drifting up and down with the length of the line (they are now anchored at the top)
Long lines now rewrap to the space available where you drag the bubble
Fixed a delayed response when reversing direction after dragging to the edge of the frame
Entering the character and subtitle tab, or changing slides, moves playback once to the selected character’s line (it stays put after you seek manually)

blocks.html: A long line is rebuilt to remain readable wherever you move the bubble. Text that fitted before the move stops at the position where the whole line still fits at the minimum scale.

sections.title: Explanations in the settings and export screens are tidier
sections.intro: Long standing explanations now open from a “?” button.

items: Notes about frame rate and resolution in video export moved into the “?” button
The pre-export summary is laid out in two columns for easier reading
In the Basic settings tab, the preset save button moved up to the heading

blocks.html: The export procedure and the available settings are unchanged; this only reduces how much you have to scroll to find them.

sections.title: SlideCast Bundle Builder was updated too
sections.intro: This release focuses on recovering an image you deleted by mistake.

blocks.html: When you delete an image, a placeholder stays in its position and offers three choices.

items.title: Undo
items.text: Restore the deleted image as it was

items.title: Regenerate here
items.text: Create a new image in the same position (a normal generation runs)

items.title: Close the gap
items.text: Give up on the image and renumber the remaining pages

blocks.alt: Bundle Builder immediately after deleting an image, showing the undo, regenerate and close-the-gap buttons
blocks.caption: The placeholder keeps the position so you can restore or rebuild the image on the spot

blocks.title: ⏳ Recovery lasts until you leave the input screen
blocks.text: Moving to the next step renumbers the pages without the deleted ones. Starting a full regeneration also discards the recovery data.

blocks.html:
Buttons to move an image left or right, and to regenerate just that image, were added to the list. Actions that are hard to undo, such as deleting or regenerating, now ask for confirmation — including inside embedded environments such as Gemini Canvas.

Image generation can be cancelled while it runs, and the screen says so when it is. The updated build opens from the Bundle Builder link inside SlideCast Studio; if you saved the old link, open it from the app instead.

blocks.title: 💰 Generation costs still apply
blocks.text: Regenerating in place, like any single-image regeneration, runs a normal generation. If you use your own API key, keep its usage charges in mind.

sections.title: Before you switch to vertical text
sections.intro: A few points worth knowing about this release.

items: Vertical writing affects how subtitles, speech bubbles, badges and text stickers are displayed. It does not rewrite or translate your text

Switching to vertical replaces the position controls with their vertical equivalents. The horizontal band height and the vertical band width are stored separately, so switching back restores the previous look
If the text does not fit the vertical band, a warning appears. Adjust by splitting the script, or changing the text size or band width
Expression and gesture material is stored per character. As it grows, backups grow too, so combine it with the selective backup added in v4.1
Existing projects open with horizontal text and 100% padding, exactly as before

sections.title: Updating to v4.2
sections.intro: If you have purchased SlideCast Studio, copy v4.2 from the same paid note shared link as before.

blocks.title: 💾 Make a backup first
blocks.text: If you want to keep your existing projects, libraries and settings, create a backup from the data save screen before updating.

blocks.html: To update the GAS edition while keeping the same URL, replace “AppBundle.html” from the v4.2 distribution folder, apply it to your existing Apps Script project, and redeploy the existing deployment as a new version.

blocks.label: Detailed update steps for the GAS edition

blocks.html: For the local HTML edition, download “SlideCast Studio v4.2 (local edition).html” and open it. A new Apps Script project or a different browser will not show your earlier data automatically; restore it from a backup instead.

sections.title: Which way should the text be read?
sections.intro: One script, two very different impressions.

blocks.html:
v4.1 “FRAME” was about where things sit within a single slide. v4.2 “TATE” is about which way the text is read. Horizontal stays as readable as ever, and material that suits vertical writing can now be set vertically — from the same script.

Vertical subtitles suit traditional Japanese subjects, literary material and a book-like presentation. Try one short slide first and compare the two directions.
